newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-HAUGLAND SURPRISE WINNER OF WOMEN'S HIGH JUMP.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-HAUGLAND SURPRISE WINNER OF WOMEN'S HIGH JUMP.

text.p: Norway's Hanne Haugland was an unexpected winner of the world women's high jump title on Sunday after clearing 1.99 metres with her fourth attempt.
Haugland, Russia's Olga Kaliturina and the Ukraine's Inga Babakova had been in flawless form throughout the competition until they got to the deciding height.
The trio failed all three of their initial efforts at 1.99 before, in a sudden-death jump-off, Haugland flew over on her extra attempt.
"I knew I could do it," Haugland said.
The Norwegian's previous best performance in a major championship was a bronze medal at the world indoor championships in March.
Haugland, 29, comes from a family of accomplished jumpers.
Her grandfather was fourth in the 1946 European Championship triple jump while her father made the finals of both the 1969 and 1971 European Championships.
Kaliturina and Babkova shared the silver medal having both cleared 1.96 on the first occasion.
It was the first time in world championship history that a jump-off has been required to determine the destination of a high jump gold medal.
The victory was Norway's second of the championship following Trine Hattestad's javelin triumph on Saturday.
